headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang answered criticism from Pope Leo XIV, head of the Catholic Church, by saying the pope is asking the right questions.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record reply tied to a widely followed safety dispute; a conciliatory statement with no new action.
importance_line: The exchange puts the leader of the Catholic Church and the head of the main AI chip supplier on the same public question of how much AI should be restricted, which matters to the many people each can reach, though neither side announced a new step.
summary: Fortune reports that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, told it on Wednesday that Pope Leo XIV, head of the Catholic Church, is "asking all the right questions" but that he was unsure what the pope meant, saying "few are doing as much in advancing AI safety" as Nvidia. The pope said at a press conference in late September that fears AI could destroy the world are not "fake news" and that he was skeptical of Nvidia's announcement about AI guardrails because Huang has argued there should be no limits and no government regulation.
notes: Reply story: Huang answers the pope's late-September press-conference remarks (exact date not given). Fortune also says Trump told the UN General Assembly the previous week that AI fears were a 'hoax'.
